actual_source_repairs.before_statement: Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $S\subset S^3$ be a smoothly embedded sphere transverse to $K$ in exactly two points. Cutting along $S$ gives two properly embedded arcs; cap each arc by an orientation-compatible simple arc on the corresponding side of $S$ to obtain oriented knots $K_1$ and $K_2$. Then the oriented isotopy class of $K$ is the connected sum $K_1\#K_2$.
actual_source_repairs.current_statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $S\subset S^3$ be a smoothly embedded sphere transverse to $K$ in exactly two points. Cutting along $S$ gives two properly embedded arcs; cap each arc by an orientation-compatible simple arc on $S$, pushed slightly into the corresponding boundary collar to obtain oriented knots $K_1$ and $K_2$. Then the oriented isotopy class of $K$ is the connected sum $K_1\#K_2$.

actual_source_repairs.before_statement: Assume full AC. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil, let $T^*$ be its image under a fixed orientation-reversing reflection of $S^3$, and let $-T^*$ denote reversal of that image's knot orientation. Then $g(T\#T)=2$ and $g(T\#(-T^*))=2$. The knot $T\#(-T^*)$ bounds a smooth ribbon disk in $B^4$, meaning a smooth properly embedded disk whose radial-height function has no interior local minima; in particular it bounds a smooth properly embedded disk and is smoothly slice.
